examples.en: Three servings of pork belly, please.

examples.ko: 이 고기는 일 인분에 만 오천 원이에요.
examples.en: This meat is 15,000 won per serving.
Two servings of galbi, please.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 일 인분은 안 팔아요.
examples.en: This restaurant doesn't sell single servings.
How much is four servings of meat?

explain: 인분은 일, 이, 삼 같은 숫자와 같이 써요: 이 인분, 삼 인분. 고기 식당 메뉴판 가격은 보통 1인분 값이에요.

dict_examples.ko: 이 만찬에는 기부자들이 제공한 3000인분의 음식이 마련됐다.
dict_examples.en: Food for 3,000 servings provided by donors was prepared for this banquet.

dict_examples.ko: 떡볶이 프랜차이즈업체가 소외 계층을 위해 떡볶이 2012인분을 나눠 주는 행사를 진행해 눈길을 끌었다.
dict_examples.en: A tteokbokki franchise drew attention by holding an event giving out 2,012 servings of tteokbokki to underprivileged groups.

explain_en: 인분 goes with the Sino-Korean numbers 일, 이, 삼: 이 인분, 삼 인분. On a BBQ restaurant menu the price is usually per one serving.

examples.en: Here are three tickets.
Movie tickets are 15,000 won.
The concert ticket is on my phone.
I get my plane ticket at the airport.
How much is this ticket? — It's 20,000 won.

explain: 티켓은 영어 ticket에서 왔어요. 콘서트, 영화, 비행기에 많이 써요. 버스나 기차는 보통 ‘표’라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: We decided that whoever arrives first would book the movie theater tickets.

explain_en: 티켓 comes from English “ticket”. It is common for concerts, movies and flights. For buses and trains people usually say 표.

dis.h: ticket; English loanword, events and shows

usage: 번 = number of times (한 번, 두 번) or number (몇 번 버스). 번호 = an ID number.

examples.en: I've been to Korea twice.
What number is this bus?

examples.ko: 저는 하루에 세 번 밥을 먹어요.
examples.en: I eat three meals a day.
Let's meet at exit number 5.
I go to the cinema twice on the weekend.

explain: 횟수는 한 번, 두 번처럼 말해요. 버스나 출구 번호는 일 번, 이 번, 삼 번처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 우리 언제 한번 같이 밥 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 약속이 아니라 인사처럼 하는 말
phrases.nuance_en: a friendly greeting rather than a real promise to meet

examples.en: Emma is third.
My seat is in the second row.
The restroom is the second door.
I sit in the first row.
I take the third bus.

explain: ‘1st’는 ‘한 번째’가 아니라 ‘첫 번째’예요. 첫만 특별해요. 두 번째, 세 번째, 네 번째는 숫자 + 번째예요.

examples.en: The baby is eight months old now.
The language school course runs three months.
The Korean course is six months long.
The visa is for three months.
I'll be in Korea for two months.

explain: 월은 달력의 달이고(삼 월), 개월은 기간이에요(삼 개월). 기간은 ‘한 달, 두 달’이라고도 해요.

explain_en: 월 is the calendar month (삼 월 = March); 개월 counts a length of time (삼 개월 = three months). You can also say 한 달, 두 달.

examples.en: I eat two bowls of rice.
My younger sibling washes the bowls.
A bowl of soup, please.
The bowls are in the kitchen.
A bowl of cold noodles is 8,000 won.

explain: 그릇은 밥이나 국을 담는 물건이에요. 음식을 셀 때도 ‘한 그릇’이라고 해요. 밥은 ‘한 공기’라고도 해요.

phrases.nuance_en: describes a person with a wide heart and big thoughts

examples.en: Two packs of ramyeon, please.
Three bags of chips for 5,000 won.
There are ten tangerines in the bag.
I buy a bag of candy at the convenience store.
Do you need a bag? — No, I'm fine.

examples.en: One pair of shoes, please.
Five pairs of socks for 10,000 won.
There are ten pairs of shoes in the shoe cabinet.
A pair of gloves, please.
A pair of sneakers is 50,000 won.

explain: 켤레는 신발, 양말, 장갑처럼 두 개가 한 쌍인 물건에 써요. 한쪽만 말할 때는 ‘한 짝’이에요.

examples.en: There are five computers.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 차가 두 대 있어요.
examples.en: We have two cars.
We have one TV at home.
A bus is coming.

examples.en: Two bicycles are in front of the door.

explain: 대는 차, 버스, 자전거, 컴퓨터, 텔레비전 같은 기계와 탈것에 써요. 사람이나 동물에는 쓰지 않아요.

explain_en: 대 counts machines and vehicles: cars, buses, bikes, computers, TVs. It is not used for people or animals.

examples.en: The quantity is on the receipt.
The order quantity is ten.
I write the quantity here.
What's the quantity? — Three.
There's only a small amount of this bread.

explain: 수량은 주문서나 영수증에서 많이 보는 글에서 쓰는 말이에요. 대화에서는 ‘몇 개예요?’가 더 자연스러워요.

dict_examples.en: Customs charges duty according to the contents and quantity of the goods.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 수량 is a written-style word you see on order forms and receipts. In conversation, “몇 개예요?” sounds more natural.
